status: the core's catalogue — the four programmes, read cell by cell from the spine's own tables. The exploration copy (exploration/plan-templates.json) is the verification copy, and a test in the core holds the two in step.
retranscribed: 2026-11-24 — from the corrected spine tables (row-index alignment of the schedule images)

source.book: Pete Pfitzinger & Philip Latter, Faster Road Racing: 5K to Half Marathon, 2nd ed. (Human Kinetics, 2015)
source.confidence: book — the four schedules were read cell by cell from the book's schedule images (spine §6.4)
source.read: cell by cell, with the printed weekly mileage as the check
source.method: the schedules print as two images per plan — the Monday–Thursday half and the Friday–Sunday-plus-volume half — and the two halves have different row heights, so they are paired by row index and then checked by sum (spine §2.3). A volume that does not sum is a finding, not a licence to adjust a cell.

units.about: every kilometre value is derived from the printed miles at 1 mile = 1.609344 km, rounded to 0.1 km; the spine's own printed kilometre bands are kept in printed_km

transcription_notes: Every day is transcribed from the spine's §2.3 table for that week; the cell text is kept verbatim in the day's 'cell' field and the parenthetical detail in 'detail'.

The spine's legend: Rest = 'Rest or cross-training'; GA*n* = general aerobic, *n* miles; GA+s = general aerobic + speed; End *n* = endurance (the long run); Prog *n* (*k* @LT) = progression long run, last *k* miles at LT pace; LT *n* = lactate threshold; VO₂ *n* = VO₂max; SR *n* = speed repetitions; Rec *n* = recovery; RP *n* = race pace.

On the race days the schedule prints a number (8, 9, 10, 11, 16, 17) that is the miles it counts for that day in the weekly total — it is not the race's own distance. The race's distance is in the day's race_distance_m and race_distance_label.
A rest or cross-training day has no distance field; it is not a zero.
volume_check.cells_mi is the sum of the printed daily miles; it reconciles when it equals the printed weekly mileage. Every week of all four programmes reconciles.
No cell anywhere has been filled from arithmetic. Where a week did not sum, it was reported as a finding and the cells were left as they stand.

rest_cross.about: not a run; the day leaves no trace in the record

ga.pace_rule: heart-rate band only — 70–81 % of max HR (62–75 % of HR reserve); the method states no pace

ga_speed.method_name: General aerobic run with speed work
ga_speed.pace_rule: heart-rate band only — 70–81 % of max HR; the speed work carries no heart-rate rule

endurance.pace_rule: 20–33 % slower than the 10K race pace at the start, 17–29 % slower than the 15K–half-marathon pace at the finish

progression_long_run.pace_rule: as the long run, then the last miles at LT pace
progression_long_run.about: the last miles of the run are at LT pace; the cell states how many

lt.pace_rule: LT pace — the pace you could race for about an hour

recovery.pace_rule: below 76 % of max HR, or 2 min/mile slower than the 15K–half-marathon race pace

tune_up_race.pace_rule: raced near maximal effort; shorter than the goal distance
tune_up_race.about: two per plan, at 4 and 2 weeks to go
